text:
If you’ve ever driven the haul road past Coldfoot, you may have seen the signs for the Toolik Field Station, just past Galbraith Lake. For more than 50 years, scientists have been braving cold and dark winters, as well as hot and mosquito-filled summers to do field research on a variety of projects, all with the goal of “inspiring an understanding of the Arctic from the ground up.” The scientists who come to Toolik are pursuing that understanding in a variety of ways in the challenging - and changing - arctic environment.

HOST: Steve Cleary

GUESTS:  Chad Diesinger - station manager for Toolik Field Station.Syndonia Bret-Harte - principal investigator and science director of TFS.Seth Beaudreault - naturalist at TFS and photographer for Toolik Naturalist Journal.

LINKS:https://www.uaf.edu/toolik/
